Heat can be changed to electrical signals and monitored by sensors.
For example, a thermostat measures the amount of heat in a room.
If the room temperature does not agree with the setting of the thermostat, either a heater or air conditioner is turned on to raise or lower the temperature.

THERMO-ELECTRONICSE
Thermo-electronics is the study of mechanical and electrical components associated with heat.
DISCUSSION
Thermo-electronics combines standard electronic circuits with special heat components to form heat circuits.
Until recently, heat and electronics were only used to measure temperatures for controlling heating and air conditioning systems.
Today, heat and electronics do a lot more.
For example, heat transducers can detect the presence of a person in a room.
Your body gives off heat and can be detected.
Heat transducers are also used in heat seeking missiles....
The missile uses the transducers to track targets.
The circuits are normal electronic circuits with the addition of components that react to heat.
What is the name of the field that combines electronics with heat?
Opto-electronics is the field that combines electronics with light, not heat.
TRY AGAIN!
Transducers are devices that change one form of energy to another. There are several types of transducers light, heat, position and motion are just a few.
TRY AGAIN!
All thermo-electronic devices are divided into two categories, generators and sensors.
A heat generator is a device that creates heat.
For example, a furnace generates heat to warm your house.
Heat generators are classified into three categories.......
I2R is heat created by electronic circuits..
Heat is generated by current flowing through a resistance.m
In a standard electronic circuit, this is unwanted heat because energy is lost.
A heating device purposely creates this heat. A thermo transducer (heating device) changes electrical energy to heat.
The second category of heat generators is friction.........
Friction generates heat by the rubbing action of two materials.
Rub your hands together quickly and you will sense the heat generated.
Heat generated by friction is normally unwanted. The friction used to create heat causes power loss and degrades mechanical parts.
The last category of generating heat is by chemical action.
Heat generated by chemical action occurs when different substances are combined, as in chemistry.
For example, fire produces chemical heat and there are packages that, when smashed, combine two substances that give off heat.
What type of heat sensor is a thermo-couple?
A heat sensor is a device that detects heat................
For example, thermostats sense room temperature and send signals to turn the furnace on and off.
Heat sensors are also classified into three categories.....
Heat sensors change heat energy into an electrical quantity.
Resistive sensors change their resistance according to the amount of heat sensed.
Examples of resistive heat sensors are thermistors and mechanical potentiometers.
Voltage sensors change their voltage output according to the amount of heat sensed.
Current sensors change their current flow according to the amount of heat sensed.
Semi-conductors devices (diodes) are current sensors.
What are the two classifications of thermo-electronic devices?
Transmitters and receivers are classifications of photoelectronic devices.

During the discovery of basic electrical phenomena in the 18th and 19th centuries, the heating properties of current flow were quickly noted.
This led to equating heat to electrical values. But, before this can be done, you must know the heating ability of a heat source.
The basic units of heating ability are the calorie (cal) and the British Thermal Unit, BTU..
One calorie is defined as the heat necessary to raise 1 gram of water 1 degree Celsius above the ambient temperature.
DEFINITION

AMBIENT - Ambient temperature is the temperature of a substance without adding or subtracting heat, the normal temperature of a substance. For example, the room that you are in may have an ambient temperature of 25 degrees Celsius.
The Calorie is a metric heat unit. Calories use grams and Celsius.
The Imperial unit of heat is the British Thermal Unit or BTU.
One BTU is defined as the heat necessary to raise 1 Lb of water, 1 degree Fahrenheit above the ambient temperature.
1 BTU is equal to 252 calories. To convert calories to BTU's multiply 252 and the calories. To convert BTU's to calories divide BTU's by calories.
How many BTU's are needed to raise 5 pounds of water 5 degrees F?
